key_insight: The paper argues that “AI-ready” biological data is not a single technical label but a set of qualities that should be defined by answering four core questions. Its main contribution is a clearer framework for thinking about what makes biological data usable, trustworthy, and valuable for AI.
problem_solved: Biological datasets are often described as AI-ready without a shared definition, making it hard to know whether they are truly suitable for machine learning. This paper addresses the ambiguity by framing the concept around a structured set of questions that data providers and AI researchers should ask.
method: Introduces a conceptual framework centered on four guiding questions for evaluating AI-readiness in biological data.
Clarifies criteria that influence whether biological data can support reliable, generalizable AI models.
Encourages alignment between data generation, curation, and downstream AI use cases.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical lens for assessing dataset quality before model training. It can improve reproducibility, reduce data-related failure modes, and help build more robust biomedical AI systems.
visual_elements: A central four-part question wheel showing the framework
A pipeline diagram from biological data generation to AI-ready data
Icons for data quality, annotation, bias, and interoperability
A checklist graphic showing readiness criteria for datasets
paper_title: Four questions for AI-ready biological data
